scenes.description: THE MARKS. Warm paper with a faint grain. A coastal section drawn in ink at the bottom third: a wedge of shore, the sea as a flat sea-blue field, and two horizontal tide marks ruled across it with light construction lines that are never cleaned up. The water rises to the upper mark, falls, and rises again - twice, in the time it takes to say the line. Nothing else is on the page.
scenes.framing: low horizon, the drawing occupying the bottom third and a wide empty margin above
scenes.movement: the water level rises and falls twice; the ruled marks stay put
scenes.overlay_notes: One ruled label only. The word TWO is not written anywhere - the motion says it.
scenes.information_role: Put the phenomenon on the page before any explanation exists.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: coastal section on a paper ground with an animated water level and ruled tide marks.

scenes.description: THE PLATE. The view leaves the shore and becomes the whole figure: a circular Earth drawn in ink at the centre of the page, the Moon small at the right margin, a light dashed axis between them. The near-side water swells toward the Moon in sea blue - obvious, expected. Then the far side swells too, drawn just as plainly, and the figure simply sits there being impossible.
scenes.framing: centred circular body, generous paper margin, Moon at the right edge
scenes.movement: ink draws on with a small overshoot and settles; the two swells grow at different moments, not together
scenes.overlay_notes: No labels on the bulges. The near one needs none and the far one is the question.
scenes.information_role: Show the familiar diagram faithfully, so the viewer recognises it as the one they were taught.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: circular body with parametric tidal-ellipse deformation, drawn-on ink, Moon glyph.

scenes.description: THE ANNOTATION. A curved vermilion arrow is drawn onto the plate sweeping outward from the far side - exactly the annotation a textbook margin would add - with a handwritten-looking label beside it. It is drawn respectfully, at full weight. Then one vermilion stroke crosses the whole annotation out. The struck-through mark stays on the page: this is a correction, not an erasure.
scenes.framing: same plate, pushed slightly left so the annotation has margin to live in
scenes.movement: the arrow draws, holds long enough to be read, then the strike crosses it in one pass
scenes.overlay_notes: The label is the only handwritten-feeling text in the video. Vermilion appears here for the first time.
scenes.information_role: Name the wrong answer, and mark it wrong without mocking it.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: curved annotation arrow with path-length reveal, plus a strike-through stroke.

scenes.description: THREE PULLS. The plate is cleared back to the bare body and axis. Three vermilion arrows are drawn along the Moon's axis - at the near ocean, at the centre of the Earth, at the far ocean - each one drawn as its clause is spoken, each visibly shorter than the last. Nothing is labelled. The lengths are the argument.
scenes.framing: body centred, arrows on the horizontal axis, Moon still at the right margin
scenes.movement: one arrow per clause, drawn left to right, each settling before the next begins
scenes.overlay_notes: Three arrows and nothing else. This is the signature device and it appears in only two scenes.
scenes.information_role: Establish that the pull is not one force but three different ones.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: three vermilion vector arrows with staggered draw-on and settle.

scenes.description: STACKED. The three arrows lift off the body and stack at the margin against a common baseline, like a figure inset, so the difference in their lengths is unmistakable at a glance. The body stays faintly behind them. Thin leader lines connect each stacked arrow back to where it came from.
scenes.framing: figure inset on the left, the body dropped to a light ghost behind
scenes.movement: the arrows travel to the baseline and align; leader lines draw after them
scenes.overlay_notes: The only moment the drawing steps outside the scene to measure itself.
scenes.information_role: Make the gradient itself visible, separated from the geometry.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: arrows animating to a shared baseline with leader lines.

scenes.description: THE SUBTRACTION. The middle arrow - the pull on the Earth itself - is taken away from all three. The near arrow keeps a short remainder pointing toward the Moon; the centre arrow vanishes to nothing; the far arrow's remainder points the other way, away from the Moon. Two outward remainders at opposite ends of the planet, arrived at by arithmetic rather than assertion. The blue swells return underneath them and fit exactly.
scenes.framing: body centred and slightly larger; the remainders are the only red left on the page
scenes.movement: each arrow shortens by the middle one's length in a single continuous move; nothing else moves
scenes.overlay_notes: No text. If this beat needs a label it has failed.
scenes.information_role: The whole video: subtract the common pull and both bulges fall out.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: vector subtraction animation with the tidal ellipse resolving underneath.

scenes.description: THE BATH. A bathtub drawn in the same ink on the same paper, sitting where the planet was, at the same scale on the page. The same three vermilion arrows are drawn on it - and this time all three are exactly the same length. The water does not move. It goes on not moving for slightly longer than is comfortable.
scenes.framing: the tub occupying the space the planet held, so the substitution is felt as well as seen
scenes.movement: arrows draw on identically; the water is the only thing in the video that refuses to respond
scenes.overlay_notes: The joke is in the equal lengths. Do not write it down.
scenes.information_role: Prove the mechanism by removing it: no gradient, no tide.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: bathtub section with three identical arrows and a flat, unmoving water line.

scenes.description: THE CAPTION. The closing line set in the plate's serif, low on the page, positioned and weighted like the caption under a figure rather than like a title. Above it the page is mostly empty, with the ghost of the body still faintly present.
scenes.framing: caption low-left in the figure position; the upper page nearly bare
scenes.movement: the line sets in without spring; the ghosted body breathes very slightly
scenes.overlay_notes: Serif, not mono. This is a page, not a readout.
scenes.information_role: Restate the mechanism as a definition the viewer can carry.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: typographic caption beat over a ghosted figure.

scenes.description: STILL LEAVING. The caption stays. The small Moon at the right margin goes on drifting outward, slowly, and is still drifting when the video ends - it never reaches the edge and it never stops. The last frame is in motion, which is the exact opposite of how the previous production closed.
scenes.framing: wide page, Moon small and near the right edge, caption held low
scenes.movement: constant slow outward drift, unresolved at the cut
scenes.overlay_notes: No end card, no logo, no subscribe prompt. The Moon is simply still going.
scenes.information_role: Leave the viewer with the consequence: this is a process, not a diagram.

required_assets.description: Bespoke TSX: the closing drift, cut while still moving.

metadata.coverage: 0.0 to 46.5s with no gaps and no overlaps; every script section is covered and the tail runs 1.63s past the last word.
metadata.variety_check: Types in order: diagram, diagram, animation, animation, diagram, animation, diagram, text_card, animation. Longest same-type run is 2 against a limit of 3, and no two consecutive scenes share a layout.
metadata.distinctness_check: Primary subjects: a shoreline · the familiar plate · a struck-out annotation · three unequal arrows · a measured inset · a subtraction · a bathtub · a caption · a departing Moon. No two are the same. The signature device (the three arrows) appears in sc-04 and sc-06 only, and sc-06 is where it earns its keep.
metadata.feasibility: Every asset is a hand-authored Remotion scene rendered locally. No image generation, no video generation, no stock - which is what makes it buildable here, where all three are unavailable.
